CreateEnvironment.name: CreateEnvironment
CreateEnvironment.documentation:
Create a new, running or stopped environment asynchronously.

Use the EventBridge for notification when the environment is "RUNNING" and therefore ready to StartSession, details.

DeleteEnvironment.name: DeleteEnvironment
DeleteEnvironment.documentation:
Delete an environment from the system.

Running environments and sessions will be stopped.

If the environment does not exist a ResourceNotFoundException will be thrown (unless the clientToken matches a previous successful request).

GetEnvironmentMetadata.name: GetEnvironmentMetadata
GetEnvironmentMetadata.documentation: Retrieve Environment information for a given EnvironmentId

ListEnvironments.name: ListEnvironments
ListEnvironments.documentation: Return the environments for a given account

ListSessions.name: ListSessions
ListSessions.documentation: Return the Sessions for a given Environment

StartSession.name: StartSession
StartSession.documentation:
Start a session connected to a running environment, either SSM or SSH (via SSM).

Multiple sessions can be connected to an environment at the same time.

If the environment is not running a ValidationException is thrown. If we are unable to connect to the environment a ConflictException is thrown.

StopEnvironment.name: StopEnvironment
StopEnvironment.documentation: Stop environment operation stops a running environment

StopSession.name: StopSession
StopSession.documentation:
Stop an existing session. Stopped sessions cannot be refreshed or restarted.

If the environment does not exist a ResourceNotFoundException will be thrown. If session is not found a ValidationException will be thrown. (REVIEW) If we are unable to contact to the environment a ConflictException will be thrown.

documentation: Managed Development Environments allow developers to easily create and reproduce as many development environments as they want - be it per software project or for individual experimentation. Using an MDE simplifies and standardizes development environments by codifying them into repeatable toolchains and by automating the creation and configuration of them on burstable compute. As MDE automates away all the manual and tedious work involved with creating and caring for development environments, developers can work more productively and focus on developing code.
